sbc.heading: Share-based compensation
sbc.text:
The Company has adopted the Plan for the purpose of providing incentives and rewards to eligible participants who contribute to the success of the Company’s operations. Shareholders, directors, and employees of the Company receive remuneration in the form of share-based awards including option, restricted stock, restricted stock unit, dividend equivalent, or other awards that are permitted under the Plan, whereby the recipients render services as consideration for such share-based compensation.

The Company measures the cost of employee services received in exchange for an award of equity instruments based on the grant-date fair value of the award and recognizes the cost over the period during which the employee is required to provide service in exchange for the award, which generally is the vesting period. The amount of cost recognized is adjusted to reflect any expected forfeitures prior to vesting. The fair value of stock award is measured at grant date’s per share closing price of the Company’s common stock, and the fair value of option is measured at grant date using the Black-Scholes pricing model, taking into account the terms and conditions upon which the share-based awards are granted.

lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Our business relies on a few customers each accounting for more than 10% of our total purchases, and interruption in any of their operations will have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
For the year ended December 31, 2024, our two largest clients accounted 87.7% and 12.3% of our total revenue, respectively.

Cost of revenues from Edward was $125,099, or 11.2% of total cost of revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $148,588 for the same period in 2024, representing a decrease of $23,489, or 15.8%, consistent with the corresponding decline in revenue from Edward.
The success of our business depends on our proprietary technologies.
Because our sales to the PRC market represent a significant part of our revenue, our business relies on a stable economic and political relationship between the U.S. and the PRC.
Our success depends on the demand for our logistics and warehousing services.

In addition, our experience in expanding non-vehicle logistics and warehousing revenue is limited, and our success in these areas will depend on our ability to develop and scale an effective salesforce to market these services to international trading companies in the U.S. and the PRC.
Clients often rely on logistics companies because developing in-house logistics and supply chain capabilities is costly, requires specialized expertise, and can lead to operational inefficiencies.
As an NVOCC, we depend on international shipping partners to transport our goods.
We depend on our OTI license to maintain our NVOCC status and maintain our logistics operations.
As an NVOCC, we rely on partnerships with various ocean carriers to transport goods.
We currently rely on our freight forwarding software, GoFreight, to manage our logistics and warehousing operations.
We rely on the capacity, reliability, and security of third-party systems and software to support our operations.
Our success will also depend on our ability to attract and retain qualified personnel to manage our existing operations as well as our future growth.
The successful operation of our business depends on our ability to attract, motivate, and retain a sufficient number of skilled employees.
We cannot predict if investors will find our Class A common stock less attractive because we may rely on these exemptions.
